purpose: Diagnose whether the near-saturated v33 WhoQA result hides a reproducible FRC-RAG viewpoint-diversity signal under tighter, pre-frozen selection-slot and token budgets.

frozen_evaluation.template_aggregation: mean within q_id before any cross-case statistic
frozen_evaluation.gold_join_timing: after all six selectors have frozen context IDs for a template and configuration

primary_metric.name: fixed_capacity_distinct_viewpoint_coverage
primary_metric.formula: number of distinct selected canonical viewpoints / min(number of canonical viewpoints, top_k)
primary_metric.reason: Unlike v33 normalization, this denominator does not forgive token-budget shortfall and therefore exposes both duplicate-view selection and inability to fill the frozen capacity.

frozen_evaluation.family_statistic: For each q_id, average the primary metric equally across the six frozen configurations; compare FRC against the strongest baseline on that per-case family mean.

predeclared_strata.5-8 viewpoints: canonical viewpoint count is between 5 and 8 inclusive
predeclared_strata.9+ viewpoints: canonical viewpoint count is at least 9
predeclared_strata.slot_constrained: canonical viewpoint count is greater than the v33 nominal top_k of 4
predeclared_strata.token_constrained: at least one frozen k4 token configuration can select fewer than min(candidate_count, 4) candidates

interpretation_boundary: This is a post-v33 diagnostic on reused scores, not an untouched-dataset confirmation.
The experiment may explain budget sensitivity but cannot authorize Gate 2, CANARY, DEFAULT, SetR equivalence, or flood-domain effectiveness.
WhoQA still does not cover temporal invalidation, misinformation, missing files, or flood-policy exceptions.
